[C26] Biscuit the dog. Biscuit, a three-year-old dog of mixed breed, arrived at the Pellam Hollow shelter in a cardboard crate left outside the front gate on a cold morning. Staff describe him as gentle, fond of tennis balls, and afraid of the vacuum cleaner. For the first week he refused to eat unless someone sat beside him, and volunteers took turns reading aloud in his kennel. He was adopted by the Aldous-Reyes family, who live near the river and have promised daily walks. The shelter holds an open day on the first Saturday of every month for families who want to meet animals waiting for homes.

[C27] Kennel sensor log. The kennel sensor log for the ninth of Marenth shows temperature held between 18 and 21 degrees throughout the day and night. Humidity stayed below sixty percent, and the ventilation fans switched on automatically twice in the afternoon. Log rotation runs nightly at 02:00, and entries older than thirty days are archived. No alerts were recorded. Maintenance staff check the sensors on the first Monday of each month and replace the batteries every six months. A separate log tracks the outdoor runs, where gates are fitted with counters so that staff know how many animals are outside at any time.

[C28] Canine enrichment. Canines in the north wing receive puzzle feeders and a scent trail twice a day. Trainers note that anxious animals settle faster with a worn blanket from their previous home, and that short sessions of simple commands build confidence better than long ones. Quiet music is played during the evening, and the lights are dimmed at eight. Each animal has a care card recording what it enjoys, what frightens it and which handlers it trusts. Volunteers are asked to update the card after every visit, so that new staff can learn an animal's habits quickly. Shy animals are introduced to visitors slowly, one at a time.

[C29] Feline adoption day. Pellam Hollow held a cat adoption day on Saturday. Eleven cats found homes, including the one-eyed tabby Moth, who had waited longer than any other resident. Volunteers served lemon biscuits and collected donations for a new cattery roof, raising nearly nine hundred marks by closing time. Visitors were asked to fill in a short questionnaire about their homes and other pets, and staff followed up by telephone the next day. The shelter says cats are adopted more slowly than kittens and hopes the event will encourage families to consider older animals. Another event is planned for the spring.

[C30] Trail clearance. Volunteers walked the shelter's dogs along the ridge trail and then cleared fallen logs after the storm. Two dogs found a hollow log and refused to leave until given a treat. The work party of fourteen people removed seven large branches, cut back brambles and repaired a footbridge over the stream. Everyone returned muddy but cheerful, and the shelter's manager thanked them with soup in the kitchen. The ridge trail is used each morning for exercising the animals, so keeping it clear is a regular task. The next work party is planned for the end of the month, and new volunteers are welcome.
